candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus VI.3 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God' — Ephrem hears in this verse the completion of the Abrahamic-Isaac-Jacob promise: the patriarchal seed becomes a peoplehood under a single covenanted Name. Tewahedo cites Ex 6:7 as the canonical formula on which both Sinai and the New-Covenant 'I will be their God and they shall be my people' (Jer 31:33; Rev 21:3) depend.
